v: An oracle[^1] concerning Nineveh.[^2] The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.[^3]
מַשָּׂ֖א נִֽינְוֵ֑ה סֵ֧פֶר חֲז֛וֹן נַח֖וּם הָאֶלְקֹשִֽׁי׃
The LORD[^4] is a jealous[^5] and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath.[^6] The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries and keeps his anger for his enemies.
אֵ֣ל קַנּ֤וֹא וְנֹקֵם֙ יְהוָ֔ה נֹקֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה וּבַ֣עַל חֵמָ֑ה נֹקֵ֤ם יְהוָה֙ לְצָרָ֔יו וְנוֹטֵ֥ר ה֖וּא לְאֹיְבָֽיו׃
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, and he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished.[^7] The LORD's way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֙יִם֙ *וגדול־**וּגְדָל־כֹּ֔חַ וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֑ה יְהוָ֗ה בְּסוּפָ֤ה וּבִשְׂעָרָה֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְעָנָ֖ן אֲבַ֥ק רַגְלָֽיו׃
He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon fades.[^8]
גּוֹעֵ֤ר בַּיָּם֙ וַֽיַּבְּשֵׁ֔הוּ וְכָל־הַנְּהָר֖וֹת הֶֽחֱרִ֑יב אֻמְלַ֤ל בָּשָׁן֙ וְכַרְמֶ֔ל וּפֶ֥רַח לְבָנ֖וֹן אֻמְלָֽל׃
The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth heaves[^9] at his presence, the world and all who live in it.
הָרִים֙ רָעֲשׁ֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת הִתְמֹגָ֑גוּ וַתִּשָּׂ֤א הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וְתֵבֵ֖ל וְכָל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃
Who can stand before his fury? Who can endure the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before him.
לִפְנֵ֤י זַעְמוֹ֙ מִ֣י יַֽעֲמ֔וֹד וּמִ֥י יָק֖וּם בַּחֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ חֲמָתוֹ֙ נִתְּכָ֣ה כָאֵ֔שׁ וְהַצֻּרִ֖ים נִתְּצ֥וּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress. He knows[^10] those who take refuge in him.
ט֣וֹב יְהוָ֔ה לְמָע֖וֹז בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה וְיֹדֵ֖עַ חֹ֥סֵי בֽוֹ׃
But with an overwhelming flood he will make a complete end of her place,[^11] and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.
וּבְשֶׁ֣טֶף עֹבֵ֔ר כָּלָ֖ה יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מְקוֹמָ֑הּ וְאֹיְבָ֖יו יְרַדֶּף־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
What are you plotting against the LORD?[^12] He will make a complete end; distress will not rise up a second time.
מַה־תְּחַשְּׁבוּן֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה כָּלָ֖ה ה֣וּא עֹשֶׂ֑ה לֹֽא־תָק֥וּם פַּעֲמַ֖יִם צָרָֽה׃
For like tangled thorns, and drunk as with their drink,[^13] they will be consumed like dry stubble, completely.
כִּ֚י עַד־סִירִ֣ים סְבֻכִ֔ים וּכְסָבְאָ֖ם סְבוּאִ֑ים אֻ֨כְּל֔וּ כְּקַ֥שׁ יָבֵ֖שׁ מָלֵֽא׃
From you has come one who plots evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.[^14]
מִמֵּ֣ךְ יָצָ֔א חֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־יְהוָ֖ה רָעָ֑ה יֹעֵ֖ץ בְּלִיָּֽעַל׃ ס
This is what the LORD says: Though they are at full strength and many, even so they will be cut down and pass away.[^15] Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.[^16]
כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם־שְׁלֵמִים֙ וְכֵ֣ן רַבִּ֔ים וְכֵ֥ן נָגֹ֖זּוּ וְעָבָ֑ר וְעִ֨נִּתִ֔ךְ לֹ֥א אֲעַנֵּ֖ךְ עֽוֹד׃
And now I will break his yoke from off you and tear off your bonds.
וְעַתָּ֕ה אֶשְׁבֹּ֥ר מֹטֵ֖הוּ מֵֽעָלָ֑יִךְ וּמוֹסְרֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲנַתֵּֽק׃

The LORD has given a command concerning you:[^17] No more descendants will bear your name.[^18] From the house of your gods I will cut off the carved image and the cast idol. I will prepare your grave, for you are worthless.[^19]
וְצִוָּ֤ה עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה לֹֽא־יִזָּרַ֥ע מִשִּׁמְךָ֖ ע֑וֹד מִבֵּ֨ית אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אַכְרִ֨ית פֶּ֧סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֛ה אָשִׂ֥ים קִבְרֶ֖ךָ כִּ֥י קַלּֽוֹתָ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *massa*, from the verb "to lift up, carry": a message "lifted up" by the prophet, or a "burden" laid on a nation. Traditionally "the burden of Nineveh".
n.2: The capital of Assyria (Jonah 1:2). Nineveh fell to the Babylonians and the Medes in 612 BC. Nahum also speaks of the fall of Thebes in Egypt, in 663 BC, as past (3:8), so he prophesied between those dates.
n.3: *Nahum* means "comfort". The town of Elkosh is unknown.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Hebrew *qanno*, "jealous, zealous", the God who demands the loyalty of his people and defends them (Exodus 20:5; 34:14). Verses 2–8 form a partial acrostic poem: their lines begin with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order, from *aleph* to *kaph*, with some gaps.
n.7: The words echo the LORD's description of himself in Exodus 34:6–7 (compare Numbers 14:18), but where Exodus has "abounding in faithful love", Nahum has "great in power".
n.8: Bashan, Carmel and Lebanon were famous for their pastures, their forests and their fruitfulness.
n.11: That is, Nineveh's place. The Hebrew is feminine.
n.12: Or "What do you think of the LORD?" The speaker may be addressing Nineveh or Judah.
n.13: The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult. Literally "For until thorns entangled, and as their drink drunk, they are consumed like dry stubble, full".
n.14: Hebrew *beliyya'al*, "worthlessness", used of what is wicked and destructive. *You* is Nineveh, and the plotter may be a king of Assyria.
n.15: The Hebrew is difficult. *They* are the Assyrians.
n.18: Literally "No more of your name will be sown".
n.19: Or "for you are contemptible", literally "for you are light", of no weight. In most English Bibles chapter 1 has a verse 15, which is 2:1 in the Hebrew.

v: Look, on the mountains, the feet of the one who brings good news,[^1] who proclaims peace![^2] Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows. For never again will the wicked one[^3] pass through you; he is completely cut off.
הִנֵּ֨ה עַל־הֶהָרִ֜ים רַגְלֵ֤י מְבַשֵּׂר֙ מַשְׁמִ֣יעַ שָׁל֔וֹם חָגִּ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה חַגַּ֖יִךְ שַׁלְּמִ֣י נְדָרָ֑יִךְ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוֹסִ֥יף ע֛וֹד *לעבור־**לַֽעֲבָר־בָּ֥ךְ בְּלִיַּ֖עַל כֻּלֹּ֥ה נִכְרָֽת׃
One who scatters[^4] has come up against you. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourself![^5] Gather all your strength!
עָלָ֥ה מֵפִ֛יץ עַל־פָּנַ֖יִךְ נָצ֣וֹר מְצֻרָ֑ה צַפֵּה־דֶ֙רֶךְ֙ חַזֵּ֣ק מָתְנַ֔יִם אַמֵּ֥ץ כֹּ֖חַ מְאֹֽד׃
For the LORD[^6] is restoring the pride of Jacob, like the pride of Israel, for plunderers have plundered them and ruined their vine branches.
כִּ֣י שָׁ֤ב יְהוָה֙ אֶת־גְּא֣וֹן יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּגְא֖וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י בְקָקוּם֙ בֹּֽקְקִ֔ים וּזְמֹרֵיהֶ֖ם שִׁחֵֽתוּ׃
The shields of his warriors are red;[^7] his soldiers are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire[^8] on the day he prepares for battle, and the spears[^9] are brandished.
מָגֵ֨ן גִּבֹּרֵ֜יהוּ מְאָדָּ֗ם אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֙יִל֙ מְתֻלָּעִ֔ים בְּאֵשׁ־פְּלָד֥וֹת הָרֶ֖כֶב בְּי֣וֹם הֲכִינ֑וֹ וְהַבְּרֹשִׁ֖ים הָרְעָֽלוּ׃
The chariots race madly through the streets; they rush back and forth in the squares. They look like torches; they dart about like lightning.
בַּֽחוּצוֹת֙ יִתְהוֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב יִֽשְׁתַּקְשְׁק֖וּן בָּרְחֹב֑וֹת מַרְאֵיהֶן֙ כַּלַּפִּידִ֔ם כַּבְּרָקִ֖ים יְרוֹצֵֽצוּ׃
He summons his nobles;[^10] they stumble as they go. They hurry to her wall, and the siege shield[^11] is set up.
יִזְכֹּר֙ אַדִּירָ֔יו יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ *בהלכותם **בַּהֲלִֽיכָתָ֑ם יְמַֽהֲרוּ֙ חֽוֹמָתָ֔הּ וְהֻכַ֖ן הַסֹּכֵֽךְ׃
The gates of the rivers are opened,[^12] and the palace melts away.
שַׁעֲרֵ֥י הַנְּהָר֖וֹת נִפְתָּ֑חוּ וְהַֽהֵיכָ֖ל נָמֽוֹג׃
It is decided:[^13] she is stripped and carried away. Her slave women moan like the sound of doves and beat their breasts.
וְהֻצַּ֖ב גֻּלְּתָ֣ה הֹֽעֲלָ֑תָה וְאַמְהֹתֶ֗יהָ מְנַֽהֲגוֹת֙ כְּק֣וֹל יוֹנִ֔ים מְתֹפְפֹ֖ת עַל־לִבְבֵהֶֽן׃
Nineveh is like a pool of water whose waters are draining away.[^14] "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one turns back.
וְנִינְוֵ֥ה כִבְרֵֽכַת־מַ֖יִם מִ֣ימֵי הִ֑יא וְהֵ֣מָּה נָסִ֔ים עִמְד֥וּ עֲמֹ֖דוּ וְאֵ֥ין מַפְנֶֽה׃
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, the wealth of every kind of precious thing.
בֹּ֥זּוּ כֶ֖סֶף בֹּ֣זּוּ זָהָ֑ב וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֙צֶה֙ לַתְּכוּנָ֔ה כָּבֹ֕ד מִכֹּ֖ל כְּלִ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה׃
Emptiness, desolation and ruin![^15] Hearts melt, knees give way, every waist trembles,[^16] and every face turns pale.[^17]
בּוּקָ֥ה וּמְבוּקָ֖ה וּמְבֻלָּקָ֑ה וְלֵ֨ב נָמֵ֜ס וּפִ֣ק בִּרְכַּ֗יִם וְחַלְחָלָה֙ בְּכָל־מָתְנַ֔יִם וּפְנֵ֥י כֻלָּ֖ם קִבְּצ֥וּ פָארֽוּר׃
Where is the lions' den now, the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness went, and the lion's cub, with no one to make them afraid?[^18]
אַיֵּה֙ מְע֣וֹן אֲרָי֔וֹת וּמִרְעֶ֥ה ה֖וּא לַכְּפִרִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַךְ֩ אַרְיֵ֨ה לָבִ֥יא שָׁ֛ם גּ֥וּר אַרְיֵ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃
The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses. He filled his caves with prey and his dens with torn flesh.
אַרְיֵ֤ה טֹרֵף֙ בְּדֵ֣י גֹֽרוֹתָ֔יו וּמְחַנֵּ֖ק לְלִבְאֹתָ֑יו וַיְמַלֵּא־טֶ֣רֶף חֹרָ֔יו וּמְעֹֽנֹתָ֖יו טְרֵפָֽה׃

Look, I am against you, declares the LORD of Armies.[^19] I will burn your chariots[^20] in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers[^21] will be heard no more.
הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֗יִךְ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְהִבְעַרְתִּ֤י בֶֽעָשָׁן֙ רִכְבָּ֔הּ וּכְפִירַ֖יִךְ תֹּ֣אכַל חָ֑רֶב וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י מֵאֶ֙רֶץ֙ טַרְפֵּ֔ךְ וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע ע֖וֹד ק֥וֹל מַלְאָכֵֽכֵה׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *mevasser*, from *basar*, "bring good news", as in Isaiah 40:9 and 52:7.
n.2: Verse 1 is 1:15 in most English Bibles, and verses 2–14 are 2:1–13. The first line is close to Isaiah 52:7, which Paul quotes in Romans 10:15.
n.4: Or "a shatterer". Some scholars read *mappets*, "a war club" (Jeremiah 51:20), with a small change to the Hebrew. The commands that follow are spoken to Nineveh, in mockery.
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: The attacking army, the Babylonians and the Medes. Their shields may have been painted red or covered with red leather.
n.8: Literally "with the fire of *peladot* are the chariots". The Hebrew word *peladot* is found only here, and its meaning is uncertain: perhaps "steel" or "torches".
n.9: Literally "the cypresses", spears with shafts of cypress wood. The Septuagint reads "the horsemen".
n.10: Literally "He remembers his mighty ones". He may be the king of Nineveh or the commander of the attackers.
n.11: Hebrew *sokhekh*, a shelter that protected soldiers attacking a city wall.
n.12: Perhaps the sluice gates of the canals and rivers around Nineveh, or the city gates by the river.
n.13: The meaning of the first words is uncertain. The older English translations took the Hebrew *hutsav*, "it is fixed", as the name of a queen, Huzzab.
n.14: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "Nineveh is like a pool of water from the days that she is, and they are fleeing". The Septuagint reads "Nineveh is like a pool of water; her waters …".
n.15: Hebrew *buqah u-mevuqah u-mevullaqah*, three words of similar sound and meaning.
n.16: Literally "there is anguish in all loins".
n.17: Literally "all faces gather a glow". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain (compare Joel 2:6).
n.18: The kings of Assyria compared themselves to lions and were proud of hunting them. Nineveh is pictured as their den, filled with prey from the nations.
n.19: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *Declares the LORD* is Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.20: Literally "her chariots". The Hebrew moves between "you" and "her".
n.21: The envoys of Assyria, who carried its demands to subject peoples (2 Kings 18:17–35; 19:9–13).

v: Woe to[^1] the city of bloodshed, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey!
ה֖וֹי עִ֣יר דָּמִ֑ים כֻּלָּ֗הּ כַּ֤חַשׁ פֶּ֙רֶק֙ מְלֵאָ֔ה לֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ טָֽרֶף׃
The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, the galloping horse and the jolting chariot!
ק֣וֹל שׁ֔וֹט וְק֖וֹל רַ֣עַשׁ אוֹפָ֑ן וְס֣וּס דֹּהֵ֔ר וּמֶרְכָּבָ֖ה מְרַקֵּדָֽה׃
Horsemen charging, flashing swords and glittering spears! Many slain, heaps of corpses, bodies without end! They stumble over the bodies.
פָּרָ֣שׁ מַעֲלֶ֗ה וְלַ֤הַב חֶ֙רֶב֙ וּבְרַ֣ק חֲנִ֔ית וְרֹ֥ב חָלָ֖ל וְכֹ֣בֶד פָּ֑גֶר וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֙צֶה֙ לַגְּוִיָּ֔ה *יכשלו **וְכָשְׁל֖וּ בִּגְוִיָּתָֽם׃
All because of the endless prostitution of the prostitute, so charming, the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her prostitution and peoples[^2] by her sorceries.[^3]
מֵרֹב֙ זְנוּנֵ֣י זוֹנָ֔ה ט֥וֹבַת חֵ֖ן בַּעֲלַ֣ת כְּשָׁפִ֑ים הַמֹּכֶ֤רֶת גּוֹיִם֙ בִּזְנוּנֶ֔יהָ וּמִשְׁפָּח֖וֹת בִּכְשָׁפֶֽיהָ׃
Look, I am against you, declares the LORD of Armies.[^4] I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.[^5]
הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֗יִךְ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְגִלֵּיתִ֥י שׁוּלַ֖יִךְ עַל־פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְהַרְאֵיתִ֤י גוֹיִם֙ מַעְרֵ֔ךְ וּמַמְלָכ֖וֹת קְלוֹנֵֽךְ׃
I will throw filth[^6] on you, treat you with contempt, and make you a spectacle.
וְהִשְׁלַכְתִּ֥י עָלַ֛יִךְ שִׁקֻּצִ֖ים וְנִבַּלְתִּ֑יךְ וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךְ כְּרֹֽאִי׃
Everyone who sees you will run from you and say, "Nineveh is devastated! Who will mourn for her?" Where can I find anyone to comfort you?[^7]
וְהָיָ֤ה כָל־רֹאַ֙יִךְ֙ יִדּ֣וֹד מִמֵּ֔ךְ וְאָמַר֙ שָׁדְּדָ֣ה נִֽינְוֵ֔ה מִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑הּ מֵאַ֛יִן אֲבַקֵּ֥שׁ מְנַחֲמִ֖ים לָֽךְ׃
Are you better than Thebes,[^8] which sat by the Nile, with water all around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?[^9]
הֲתֵֽיטְבִי֙ מִנֹּ֣א אָמ֔וֹן הַיֹּֽשְׁבָה֙ בַּיְאֹרִ֔ים מַ֖יִם סָבִ֣יב לָ֑הּ אֲשֶׁר־חֵ֣יל יָ֔ם מִיָּ֖ם חוֹמָתָֽהּ׃
Cush and Egypt were her strength, without limit; Put and the Libyans were among her helpers.[^10]
כּ֥וּשׁ עָצְמָ֛ה וּמִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֵ֣ין קֵ֑צֶה פּ֣וּט וְלוּבִ֔ים הָי֖וּ בְּעֶזְרָתֵֽךְ׃
Yet she too went into exile; she went into captivity. Her infants too were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
גַּם־הִ֗יא לַגֹּלָה֙ הָלְכָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔בִי גַּ֧ם עֹלָלֶ֛יהָ יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ כָּל־חוּצ֑וֹת וְעַל־נִכְבַּדֶּ֙יהָ֙ יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֔ל וְכָל־גְּדוֹלֶ֖יהָ רֻתְּק֥וּ בַזִּקִּֽים׃
You too will become drunk;[^11] you will go into hiding.[^12] You too will seek refuge from the enemy.
גַּם־אַ֣תְּ תִּשְׁכְּרִ֔י תְּהִ֖י נַֽעֲלָמָ֑ה גַּם־אַ֛תְּ תְּבַקְשִׁ֥י מָע֖וֹז מֵאוֹיֵֽב׃
All your fortresses are like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, the figs fall into the mouth of the eater.
כָּ֨ל־מִבְצָרַ֔יִךְ תְּאֵנִ֖ים עִם־בִּכּוּרִ֑ים אִם־יִנּ֕וֹעוּ וְנָפְל֖וּ עַל־פִּ֥י אוֹכֵֽל׃
Look, your troops are women in your midst.[^13] The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has devoured your gate bars.
הִנֵּ֨ה עַמֵּ֤ךְ נָשִׁים֙ בְּקִרְבֵּ֔ךְ לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ פָּת֥וֹחַ נִפְתְּח֖וּ שַׁעֲרֵ֣י אַרְצֵ֑ךְ אָכְלָ֥ה אֵ֖שׁ בְּרִיחָֽיִך׃
Draw water for the siege! Strengthen your fortresses! Go into the clay and tread the mortar! Take hold of the brick mold![^14]
מֵ֤י מָצוֹר֙ שַֽׁאֲבִי־לָ֔ךְ חַזְּקִ֖י מִבְצָרָ֑יִךְ בֹּ֧אִי בַטִּ֛יט וְרִמְסִ֥י בַחֹ֖מֶר הַחֲזִ֥יקִי מַלְבֵּֽן׃
There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you off. It will devour you as the hopping locust does.[^15] Multiply like the hopping locust! Multiply like the swarming locust!
שָׁ֚ם תֹּאכְלֵ֣ךְ אֵ֔שׁ תַּכְרִיתֵ֣ךְ חֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְלֵ֖ךְ כַּיָּ֑לֶק הִתְכַּבֵּ֣ד כַּיֶּ֔לֶק הִֽתְכַּבְּדִ֖י כָּאַרְבֶּֽה׃
You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The hopping locust strips the land[^16] and flies away.
הִרְבֵּית֙ רֹֽכְלַ֔יִךְ מִכּוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם יֶ֥לֶק פָּשַׁ֖ט וַיָּעֹֽף׃
Your guards are like the swarming locust, your officials[^17] like swarms of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where they are.
מִנְּזָרַ֙יִךְ֙ כָּֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְטַפְסְרַ֖יִךְ כְּג֣וֹב גֹּבָ֑י הַֽחוֹנִ֤ים בַּגְּדֵרוֹת֙ בְּי֣וֹם קָרָ֔ה שֶׁ֤מֶשׁ זָֽרְחָה֙ וְנוֹדַ֔ד וְלֹֽא־נוֹדַ֥ע מְקוֹמ֖וֹ אַיָּֽם׃
Your shepherds are asleep, king of Assyria; your nobles lie down to rest.[^18] Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
נָמ֤וּ רֹעֶ֙יךָ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר יִשְׁכְּנ֖וּ אַדִּירֶ֑יךָ נָפֹ֧שׁוּ עַמְּךָ֛ עַל־הֶהָרִ֖ים וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּֽץ׃
There is no relief for your injury; your wound is fatal. All who hear the news about you clap their hands over you, for who has not felt your endless cruelty?[^19]
אֵין־כֵּהָ֣ה לְשִׁבְרֶ֔ךָ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֶ֑ךָ כֹּ֣ל ׀ שֹׁמְעֵ֣י שִׁמְעֲךָ֗ תָּ֤קְעוּ כַף֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֗י עַל־מִ֛י לֹֽא־עָבְרָ֥ה רָעָתְךָ֖ תָּמִֽיד׃

n.1: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning for the dead ("Alas!", 1 Kings 13:30). The prophets use it to announce disaster, and in that sense it is translated "Woe to".
n.3: Nineveh is pictured as a prostitute and a sorceress, who lured nations into her power and sold them into slavery.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *Declares the LORD* is Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.5: The public shaming of an unfaithful woman (Jeremiah 13:22, 26; Ezekiel 16:37).
n.6: Hebrew *shiqqutsim*, "detestable things", a word often used of idols.
n.8: Hebrew *No-amon*, "city of Amon", the great city of Upper Egypt, sacked by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal in 663 BC.
n.9: Literally "whose rampart was the sea, from the sea her wall". *The sea* and *the Nile* (literally "the Niles", its channels) are the great river.
n.10: Literally "were your help". Cush, the land on the upper Nile, ruled Egypt at the time. Put was perhaps a region of Libya.
n.11: Drunk with the cup of the LORD's anger (Obadiah 16; Jeremiah 25:15–29).
n.12: Or "you will faint". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.13: That is, weak and unable to fight (Isaiah 19:16; Jeremiah 50:37). The Hebrew is feminine throughout verses 11–17, addressing Nineveh.
n.14: Or "the brick kiln". The walls of Nineveh were built of sun-dried brick. The commands are mockery: no preparations will save the city.
n.15: Hebrew *yeleq*, the "hopping locust" of Joel 1:4. Also in verse 16. The *swarming locust* is *arbeh*, the usual word for locust (also in verse 17). In verse 17, *swarms of locusts* is Hebrew *gov govai*.
n.16: Or "sheds its skin". *The land* is added.
n.17: Hebrew *minnezarayikh* and *tafsarayikh*, both rare words for officials, perhaps borrowed from the Assyrian language (Jeremiah 51:27).
n.18: The rulers of Assyria are asleep in death. *Lie down to rest* is literally "dwell". Some scholars read "sleep", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.19: Literally "for on whom has your evil not passed continually?" Like the book of Jonah, which also concerns Nineveh, Nahum ends with a question.
